io.flic.flic2libandroid

Class Flic2Button

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.flic.flic2libandroid.Flic2Button

  • public class Flic2Button
extends Object
    Flic 2 button class.

    This class represents a paired Flic 2 button.

    This class cannot be instantiated directly. Instead get an object using Flic2Manager.startScan(Flic2ScanCallback) or Flic2Manager.getButtons()

        public static final int CONNECTION_STATE_DISCONNECTED
        The button is in the disconnected state. No connection attempt is currently in progress. Call connect() if you would like to establish a connection as soon as the button comes in range and advertises.

      • CONNECTION_STATE_CONNECTING

        public static final int CONNECTION_STATE_CONNECTING
        The manager is waiting for the button to come in range and advertise, at which time it should automatically connect. Note that this state is also possible when Bluetooth is turned off, in which case it means the manager will wait for Bluetooth to become turned on and then connect.

      • connect

        public void connect()
        Puts the button object in the connect state.

        Attempts to connect to the button. If Bluetooth is off, the button is not available, due to either being out of range or not currently advertising, then the button will be connected once it becomes available since this call will not time out, also called a pending connection.

        If the connection drops, a reconnection attempt will be made automatically.

        This state is exited by calling the disconnectOrAbortPendingConnection() method.

        If the button already is in this state, or isUnpaired() is true, this method does nothing.

      • disconnectOrAbortPendingConnection

        public void disconnectOrAbortPendingConnection()
        Puts the button object in the disconnect state.

        If the connection is established, it is disconnected and the Flic2ButtonListener.onDisconnect(io.flic.flic2libandroid.Flic2Button) callback will later be run. Else it aborts a pending connection request, if there is one.

      • getConnectionState

        public int getConnectionState()
        Gets the connection state of this button.

        Returns one of CONNECTION_STATE_DISCONNECTED, CONNECTION_STATE_CONNECTING, CONNECTION_STATE_CONNECTED_STARTING and CONNECTION_STATE_CONNECTED_READY.

        To get the expected results, run this on the thread that is associated with the manager's Handler.

        Returns:
        the connection state

      • addListener

        public void addListener(Flic2ButtonListener listener)
        Adds a button event listener.

        The processing order of events will be the same order as the listeners are added. If a listener is added while a callback is currently executing, the new listener will also be called.

        If the listener is already added, this method does nothing.

        NOTE: remember to remove the listener when appropriate. If you add a listener in an onCreate method for example in an Activity, remember to always remove it in the corresponding onDestroy method.

        Parameters:
        listener - the listener

      • removeListener

        public void removeListener(Flic2ButtonListener listener)
        Removes a button event listener.

        If a listener is removed while a callback is currently executing, the removed listener will not be called.

        Parameters:
        listener - the listener

      • setName

        public void setName(String name)
        Sets a new name of the button.

        This sets a new name of the button. The new name will be written to the button's internal memory. If the button is disconnected it will sync when it later connects.

        Assuming this method is called on the manager's handler's thread, the name returned by getName() will immediately reflect the newly set name.

        If isUnpaired() is true however, this method will do nothing.

        Parameters:
        name - a name which will be truncated so that it takes up at most 23 bytes (after UTF-8 conversion), must not be null

      • setAutoDisconnectTime

        public void setAutoDisconnectTime(int numSeconds)
        Sets how long the connection should stay alive.

        This value controls when the button should automatically disconnect due to inactivity. Use this to preserve battery life, but it might affect latency.

        A value of 511 means infinite. Otherwise the button will automatically disconnect after the specified number of seconds.

        The value is not persistent between app restarts, so if this feature is used this method should be called after a new button has been paired as well as upon app start.

        Parameters:
        numSeconds - number of seconds, between 40 and 511

      • isUnpaired

        public boolean isUnpaired()
        Checks if a button is unpaired.

        This value becomes true when Flic2Manager.forgetButton(Flic2Button) or Flic2ButtonListener.onUnpaired(Flic2Button) is called.

        At that point this object becomes "dead" and connect() will do nothing. Pair the button again with Flic2Manager.startScan(Flic2ScanCallback) to get a new object.

        Returns:
        true if unpaired

      • getReadyTimestamp

        public long getReadyTimestamp()
        Gets the button's timestamp when it became ready.

        This is the same value that was latest sent in Flic2ButtonListener.onReady(Flic2Button, long). Might return an unexpected result if called from another thread than the manager's handler's thread if the button just reconnected.

        Returns:
        the timestamp in milliseconds since the button booted

      • getPressCount

        public int getPressCount()
        Gets press count.

        This property specifies how many times the button has been toggled at any given time since boot. This will register all down events as well as the up events, which means that if you want to know how many times it has been clicked then you have to divide this number by two. Also, this property will always contain the last known registered value, meaning that if the button has been pressed while not being within proximity then the property will of course not be up to date. It will be updated as soon as the button connects the next time.

        Returns:
        The press count

      • getLastKnownBatteryLevel

        public BatteryLevel getLastKnownBatteryLevel()

        It can return null in case the button was rebooted and the value has not yet been fetched.

        Returns:
